review_candidates.description: Who are we? We are a team of driven individuals who strongly believe in the positive impact gaming and AI will have on the learning world. Today, we're helping enterprise businesses in high-risk industries move to immersive, gamified safety training that far outperforms its traditional counterparts, so every frontline worker goes home safely. If you strive to work in a creative and high-output environment, read on. Why this role exists Customers increasingly ask us for video: a short film to launch a new campaign, a reconstruction of an incident for a toolbox talk, a scene to sit inside a training module. Today those requests compete for time with everything else our delivery team does. We want one person who owns them end to end. You'll use AI video tools alongside traditional editing to turn a brief into a finished, multi-shot film, quickly and to a standard a safety director at a global operator would put in front of thousands of workers. You'll sit in our Delivery team, working directly with the people who run our customer programmes. What you'll do Make videos for customers on demand. Take a brief from Delivery (often a procedure, a rule or an incident report), shape it into a storyboard, and deliver a finished film, typically one to five minutes long Build video into our training modules. Create scenes, openers and incident reconstructions that sit inside Pixaera's decision-led modules, set in the worlds our learners know: oil and gas facilities, open-pit mines, construction sites and data centres Create promotional content. Produce short films our customers use to launch programmes to their workforce, and that we use to show what Pixaera can do Make internal video. Product walkthroughs, explainers and team content when we need them Own the craft from shot to cut. Generate, select and edit footage; keep characters, PPE, equipment and environments consistent from shot to shot; add voiceover, sound and captions; and version for different languages and channels Make it repeatable. Turn what works into prompts, presets and templates so the tenth video takes a fraction of the time the first one did In your first six months, success looks like owning the customer video queue, shipping to an agreed turnaround, and building a library of reusable looks and characters the whole team can draw on. The hard parts AI video still fights you on continuity, and our subject matter is unforgiving: a worker's PPE, a valve or a permit procedure has to be right in every shot, or a safety professional will spot it immediately. Requests also arrive on customer timelines, so you'll sometimes juggle several briefs at once and need to push back, scope down or ask for clarity early. Requirements What we're looking for The single most important thing is your portfolio. We're not looking for impressive seven-second AI clips. We want to see multi-shot work that runs for minutes and holds together, because that's what proves you can edit and tell a story, not just generate. Multi-shot, minutes-long video you've made. At least one or two pieces that run a minute or more and are built from many shots, with AI-generated footage as a significant part of the work Strong editing instincts. Pacing that keeps people watching, framing that puts attention where it belongs, and continuity that holds across cuts: same character, same kit, same light, same world Fluency with current AI video and image tools, and the judgement to know when a shot needs regenerating, fixing in the edit or replacing altogether A solid traditional editor's toolkit, such as Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut, plus working comfort with sound, voiceover and captions Storytelling from a brief. You can take a dry document and find the scene, the tension and the moment that makes someone care Speed with judgement. You can turn work round quickly without letting quality slip, and you're comfortable taking feedback from customers through our Delivery team You don't need a background in health and safety. You do need to care about getting the details right, because our audience will notice a missing hard hat. Benefits How do we support and benefit our employees: Competitive salary and stock options — everyone shares in what we're building 25 days holiday + public holidays Fully equipped setup from day one (no waiting for laptops) Regular company offsites and team socials A flat, transparent culture with direct access to leadership At Pixaera, we're committed to building a workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and empowered to thrive. We believe that diverse perspectives fuel creativity and innovation, which is why we celebrate individuality and foster an environment of inclusion and belonging. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer — discrimination of any kind has no place here. No matter your background, identity, or lived experience, you're welcome at Pixaera.

review_candidates.title: Specialist, Programs – Budget Monitoring, Compliance & Deliverables
review_candidates.description: Job Summary The Specialist, Programs – Budget Monitoring, Compliance & Deliverables ensures effective budget planning, expenditure monitoring, compliance oversight, and timely achievement of organizational and project deliverables. The role serves as a key coordination point between finance, operations, procurement, and program teams. The Specialist designs, maintains, and improves budget tracking systems, analyzing financial performance, monitoring compliance with internal policies and donor requirements, and ensuring that agreed deliverables are completed on time and to the required quality standards. The position requires strong analytical, coordination, and reporting skills, with a focus on accountability, risk identification, and supporting evidence-based decision-making. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation. Main Tasks And Responsibilities Develop, maintain, and continuously improve budget tracking tools, dashboards, and financial monitoring systems for departments, projects, and the organization. Monitor budget performance against approved plans, analyze variances, and prepare regular budget-versus-actual reports with clear recommendations for corrective action. Track expenditure trends and resource utilization rates to promote efficient and accountable use of funds. Review spending requests to ensure alignment with approved budgets and funding allocations. Coordinate budget revisions and reallocations while maintaining proper documentation and approval processes. Establish and maintain robust systems for tracking organizational, departmental, and project deliverables, milestones, and deadlines. Monitor progress against action plans and work with responsible teams to identify delays, risks, and bottlenecks, and recommend mitigation measures. Maintain accurate deliverable registers, action trackers, and performance monitoring tools. Prepare periodic status reports on budget performance, compliance, and deliverables achievement for management and stakeholders. Monitor compliance with organizational policies, procedures, donor requirements, contractual obligations, and regulatory standards. Ensure appropriate documentation is maintained to support internal and external audits and compliance reviews. Coordinate and facilitate meetings related to budget reviews, compliance monitoring, and performance tracking; follow up on action items and decisions. Identify financial, compliance, and delivery risks and recommend mitigation strategies; support implementation of risk management actions. Contribute to process improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing efficiency, accountability, and internal controls. Serve as a liaison between finance, operations, procurement, and program teams to facilitate effective coordination and information flow. Analyze expenditure and spending trends across finance, logistics, and program data to generate insight and recommendations that support the timely and effective implementation of projects. Advise budget holders and program teams on corrective actions and interpret donor compliance requirements to inform decision-making. Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Public Administration, or a related field. A master’s degree or professional certification (e.g., CPA, ACCA, or PMP) is an advantage. Minimum of 5-7 years of relevant experience in budget management, financial monitoring, compliance, or program/project coordination, preferably in the non-profit, humanitarian, or development sector. Strong knowledge of budget management, financial reporting, compliance frameworks, and donor reporting requirements, including the ability to design and improve monitoring tools and dashboards. Proven experience developing and using budget tracking tools, dashboards, and performance monitoring systems. Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail. Demonstrated ability to coordinate across multiple departments and manage competing priorities under tight deadlines. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear reports and present financial and performance information effectively. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel (advanced level) and familiarity with financial management or ERP systems. High level of integrity, accountability, and commitment to compliance and ethical standards. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, multicultural environment.
